In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HPS proteins are essential for the biogenesis of melano-lysosomal organelles.

the HPS-1 gene product is required for the normal trafficking of tyrosinase and Tyrp1 to melanosomes, whereas the HPS-3 gene product is required to maintain the normal trafficking of LAMP1, LAMP3, and Dct to melanosomes.

the HPS-1 gene product is required for normal expression and trafficking of Tyrp1, Dct/Tyr2, LAMPs, and HPS-1 itself, whereas the HPS-2 and HPS-4 gene products are essential for the normal expression and trafficking only of HPS-2 itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPS1, AP3B1 and HPS3 are involved in the biogenesis of melanosome, platelet dense granule and lysosome, but they have different functions and are not interchangeable in their function.
the three HPS subtypes exhibit distinct defects in melanosome biogesnesis, and the expression of the HPS1 and HPS3 proteins are not affected in HPS- 2 and HPS-1 cells, respectively.

The main takeaway from our work is that
HPS1 and HPS3 are required for the biogenesis of melanasomes and other intracellular organelles.
HPS-1 is a disease of melanosome biogenesis and HPS-1 patients should be considered for gene therapy trials.
there is no single protein or pathway that is defective in HPS.
